chapters.title: The Word of the Cross
chapters.html:
1 Corinthians 1

Greeting

1Paul, called to be an apostle of Christ Jesus by the will of God, and our brother Sosthenes,

2to the church of God that is in Corinth, to those made holy in Christ Jesus, called to be saints, together with all those who in every place call on the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, their Lord and ours:

3grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

Thanksgiving

4I always thank my God for you because of the grace of God that was given to you in Christ Jesus,

5that in every way you were made rich in Him, in all speech and all knowledge,

6just as the testimony about Christ was confirmed among you,

7so that you are not lacking in any gift as you wait for the revealing of our Lord Jesus Christ.

8He will also keep you strong to the end, blameless on the day of our Lord Jesus Christ.

9God is faithful, by whom you were called into fellowship with His Son, Jesus Christ our Lord.

Divisions in the Church

10I appeal to you, brothers, by the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that all of you agree, and that there be no divisions among you, but that you be knit together in the same mind and the same judgment.

11For it has been made clear to me by Chloe's people, my brothers, that there are quarrels among you.

12What I mean is this: each of you says, "I belong to Paul," or "I belong to Apollos," or "I belong to Cephas," or "I belong to Christ."

13Is Christ divided? Was Paul crucified for you? Or were you baptized in the name of Paul?

14I thank God that I baptized none of you except Crispus and Gaius,

15so that no one can say that you were baptized in my name.

16I did baptize the household of Stephanas as well; beyond that, I do not know whether I baptized anyone else.

17For Christ did not send me to baptize but to preach the gospel, and not with wisdom of words, so that the cross of Christ would not be emptied of its power.

The Foolishness of God

18For the word of the cross is foolishness to those who are perishing, but to us who are being saved it is the power of God.

19For it is written:
"I will destroy the wisdom of the wise,
and the understanding of the understanding I will set aside."

20Where is the wise man? Where is the scribe? Where is the debater of this age? Has not God made foolish the wisdom of the world?

21For since, in the wisdom of God, the world did not know God through its wisdom, it pleased God through the foolishness of what we preach to save those who believe.

22Jews ask for signs and Greeks seek wisdom,

23but we preach Christ crucified: a stumbling block to Jews and foolishness to Gentiles,

24but to those who are called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ the power of God and the wisdom of God.

25For the foolishness of God is wiser than men, and the weakness of God is stronger than men.

26Consider your calling, brothers: not many of you were wise by human standards, not many were powerful, not many were of noble birth.

27But God chose what is foolish in the world to shame the wise; God chose what is weak in the world to shame the strong;

28God chose what is low and despised in the world, the things that are not, to bring to nothing the things that are,

29so that no human being might boast before God.

30It is from Him that you are in Christ Jesus, who became for us wisdom from God, and righteousness and holiness and redemption,

31so that, as it is written, "Let him who boasts boast in the Lord."

Notes

  • vv17–18 "not with wisdom of words… the word of the cross is foolishness" — ouk en sophia logou… ho logos ho tou staurou: Paul refuses one kind of logos, wisdom made of words, and preaches another, the logos of the cross, the word of John 1:1. The cross is mōria, foolishness, to Greeks and skandalon, a stumbling block, to Jews (v23), the word of a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense (Romans 9:33).

  • vv19–20 "I will destroy the wisdom of the wise… Where is the wise man? Where is the scribe?" — Isaiah 29:14 in the Greek, I will destroy the wisdom of the wise, where the Hebrew has the wisdom of their wise men will perish. Its last word in both is hidden; Paul has I will set aside. Where is the scribe? answers the Greek of Isaiah 33:18, Where are the scribes?, spoken over the fall of the Assyrian.

  • v28 "the things that are not, to bring to nothing the things that are" — ta mē onta, the words of Romans 4:17, the God who calls into being what does not exist. The God who calls what is not chooses what is not.

  • vv26–31 "not many wise… not many powerful… not many of noble birth… Let him who boasts boast in the Lord" — Jeremiah 9:23–24: Let not the wise man boast in his wisdom; let not the mighty man boast in his might; let not the rich man boast in his riches; but let him who boasts boast in this, that he understands and knows Me. Paul's three are Jeremiah's wise and mighty, with noble birth in place of riches, and the boast is still in the Lord, which in Paul's sentence follows straight on from Christ Jesus (v30).

chapters.title: The Wisdom of God in a Mystery
chapters.html:
1 Corinthians 2

Christ Crucified

1When I came to you, brothers, I did not come with lofty speech or wisdom as I proclaimed to you the testimony of God.

2For I decided to know nothing among you except Jesus Christ, and Him crucified.

3I came to you in weakness and in fear and with much trembling,

4and my speech and my preaching were not with the persuasion of wisdom, but with a demonstration of the Spirit and of power,

5so that your faith would not rest on the wisdom of men but on the power of God.

The Hidden Wisdom

6Yet among the mature we do speak wisdom, though not a wisdom of this age or of the rulers of this age, who are being brought to nothing.

7We speak God's wisdom in a mystery, the hidden wisdom that God appointed beforehand, before the ages, for our glory.

8None of the rulers of this age understood it, for if they had, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory.

9But, as it is written:
"What no eye has seen and no ear has heard,
and what has not come into the heart of man,
what God has prepared for those who love Him" —

10these things God has revealed to us through the Spirit. For the Spirit searches everything, even the depths of God.

11For who knows a person's thoughts except the spirit of that person, which is in him? So also no one has known the thoughts of God except the Spirit of God.

12We have not received the spirit of the world, but the Spirit who is from God, so that we may understand what God has freely given us.

13These things we also speak, not in words taught by human wisdom but in words taught by the Spirit, explaining spiritual things in spiritual words.

14The natural person does not accept the things of the Spirit of God, for they are foolishness to him, and he cannot understand them, because they are judged spiritually.

15The spiritual person judges all things, but is himself judged by no one.

16"For who has known the mind of the Lord, so as to instruct Him?" But we have the mind of Christ.

Notes

  • vv6–8 "the rulers of this age, who are being brought to nothing… they would not have crucified the Lord of glory" — hoi archontes tou aiōnos toutou can be the men who put Jesus to death, the high priests and Pilate, or the unseen powers behind them, as Romans 8:38 counts rulers, archai, among the powers that cannot separate us from the love of God. The Lord of glory is a title of God in 1 Enoch, the Holy and Great One, the Lord of glory, the Eternal King (1 Enoch 25:3), and Psalm 24 calls Him the King of glory. Paul gives it to the one who was crucified.

  • v9 "What no eye has seen and no ear has heard" — as it is written, but no verse reads exactly so. The nearest is Isaiah 64:4, no ear has perceived, no eye has seen a God besides You, who acts for the one who waits for Him; what has not come into the heart is in the Greek of Isaiah 65:17. Paul has for those who love Him where Isaiah has for the one who waits for Him.

  • vv13–15 "spiritual things in spiritual words… The natural person… The spiritual person" — pneumatikois pneumatika synkrinontes can be read explaining spiritual things in spiritual words, to spiritual people, or comparing spiritual things with spiritual. Psychikos, natural, is from psychē, the life every human being has; pneumatikos, spiritual, from pneuma, the Spirit God gives. The same pair returns in 15:44, a natural body… a spiritual body.

  • v16 "who has known the mind of the Lord… But we have the mind of Christ" — Isaiah 40:13 in the Greek, which Paul quoted in Romans 11:34 to say no one has. Here he answers it: the mind of the Lord, YHWH in Isaiah, is given in the mind of Christ.

chapters.title: God's Field, God's Building
chapters.html:
1 Corinthians 3

Still of the Flesh

1But I, brothers, could not speak to you as spiritual people, but as people of the flesh, as infants in Christ.

2I gave you milk to drink, not solid food, for you were not yet able to take it. Even now you are not able,

3for you are still of the flesh. While there is jealousy and strife among you, are you not of the flesh, and living in a merely human way?

4For when one says, "I belong to Paul," and another, "I belong to Apollos," are you not merely human?

Servants of God

5What, then, is Apollos? What is Paul? Servants through whom you came to believe, as the Lord gave to each.

6I planted, Apollos watered, but God gave the growth.

7So neither the one who plants nor the one who waters is anything, but only God, who gives the growth.

8The one who plants and the one who waters are one, and each will receive his own wages according to his own labor.

9For we are God's fellow workers; you are God's field, God's building.

The Foundation

10According to the grace of God given to me, like a skilled master builder I laid a foundation, and someone else is building on it. Let each one take care how he builds on it.

11For no one can lay a foundation other than the one already laid, which is Jesus Christ.

12If anyone builds on the foundation with gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, straw,

13each one's work will become plain, for the Day will show it, because it will be revealed by fire, and the fire itself will test what sort of work each one has done.

14If the work that anyone has built on the foundation survives, he will receive wages.

15If anyone's work is burned up, he will suffer loss, though he himself will be saved, but only as through fire.

God's Temple

16Do you not know that you are God's temple and that the Spirit of God lives in you?

17If anyone destroys God's temple, God will destroy him. For God's temple is holy, and you are that temple.

All Things Are Yours

18Let no one deceive himself. If anyone among you thinks he is wise in this age, let him become a fool, so that he may become wise.

19For the wisdom of this world is foolishness with God. For it is written, "He catches the wise in their own craftiness,"

20and again, "The Lord knows the thoughts of the wise, that they are empty."

21So let no one boast in men. For all things are yours,

22whether Paul or Apollos or Cephas or the world or life or death or the present or the future — all are yours,

23and you are Christ's, and Christ is God's.

Notes

  • vv10–11 "I laid a foundation… no one can lay a foundation other than the one already laid, which is Jesus Christ" — Isaiah's foundation, I am laying in Zion a stone, a tested stone, a precious cornerstone, a sure foundation (Isaiah 28:16), the stone Paul named in Romans 9:33. Paul laid it at Corinth; what others build on it, the fire of the Day will test.

  • vv16–17 "you are God's temple… you are that temple" — naos, the inner sanctuary where God dwelt, not the whole temple court. You is plural all through: the church together is where the Spirit of God lives. Phtheirei… phtherei, destroys… will destroy, is one verb, the punishment matching the deed.

  • vv19–20 "He catches the wise in their own craftiness… The Lord knows the thoughts of the wise, that they are empty" — Job 5:13, in words closer to the Hebrew than to the Greek, and Psalm 94:11, which reads the thoughts of man, that they are a breath: Paul has the wise where the psalm has man. Mataioi, empty, is the word of Romans 1:21, their thinking became empty.

  • vv21–23 "all are yours, and you are Christ's, and Christ is God's" — the slogans of 1:12 turned around. They said I am Paul's, I am Apollos'; Paul answers that Paul and Apollos belong to them, and they belong to no one but Christ.

chapters.title: Fools for Christ's Sake
chapters.html:
1 Corinthians 4

Stewards of the Mysteries

1This is how people should reckon us: as servants of Christ and stewards of the mysteries of God.

2What is required of stewards, moreover, is that each be found faithful.

3But to me it matters very little that I should be judged by you or by any human day of judgment. I do not even judge myself.

4For I know of nothing against myself, but I am not justified by that. The one who judges me is the Lord.

5So do not pronounce judgment before the time, before the Lord comes. He will bring to light what is hidden in darkness and make known the purposes of hearts, and then each one will receive his praise from God.

Nothing Beyond What Is Written

6I have applied all this to myself and Apollos for your sake, brothers, so that you may learn from us the saying "Nothing beyond what is written," and none of you may be puffed up in favor of one man against another.

7For who makes you different from anyone else? What do you have that you did not receive? If you received it, why do you boast as if you had not?

8Already you have all you want! Already you have become rich! Without us you have become kings! I wish you really were kings, so that we might be kings with you.

9For I think God has put us apostles on display last of all, like men sentenced to death, because we have become a spectacle to the world, to angels and to men.

10We are fools for Christ's sake, but you are wise in Christ. We are weak, but you are strong. You are held in honor, but we in disgrace.

11To this very hour we go hungry and thirsty, we are poorly clothed and beaten and homeless,

12we labor, working with our own hands. When we are reviled, we bless; when we are persecuted, we endure;

13when we are slandered, we answer kindly. We have become like the scum of the world, the refuse of all things, to this day.

My Beloved Children

14I do not write these things to shame you, but to warn you as my beloved children.

15For though you may have ten thousand guardians in Christ, you do not have many fathers. In Christ Jesus I became your father through the gospel.

16So I urge you, be imitators of me.

17That is why I sent you Timothy, my beloved and faithful child in the Lord, to remind you of my ways in Christ Jesus, as I teach them everywhere in every church.

18Some of you have become puffed up, as though I were not coming to you.

19But I will come to you soon, if the Lord wills, and I will find out not the talk of these puffed-up people but their power.

20For the kingdom of God is not a matter of talk but of power.

21Which do you want? Shall I come to you with a rod, or with love and a spirit of gentleness?

Notes

  • vv3–5 "any human day of judgment… I am not justified by that… then each one will receive his praise from God" — anthrōpinēs hēmeras, word for word a human day, set against the Day that the fire will reveal (3:13). A clear conscience does not acquit: dedikaiōmai, I am justified, the court verb of Romans, belongs to the Lord's verdict alone. His praise from God is the end of Romans 2:29, his praise is not from people but from God.

  • vv6, 18–19 "Nothing beyond what is written… puffed up" — four Greek words, mē hyper ha gegraptai, and the meaning has never been settled: keep within the Scriptures Paul has just quoted (1:19, 31; 3:19–20), or within what Scripture says at all. Physioō, puff up: six of its eight uses in the New Testament are in this letter, down to love is not puffed up (13:4).

  • vv12–13 "When we are reviled, we bless; when we are persecuted, we endure" — the teaching of Jesus lived out: bless those who curse you, pray for those who mistreat you (Luke 6:28), which Paul had given the Romans as Bless those who persecute you (Romans 12:14).
